postmortem.root_cause: Unplanned re-replication activity triggered by NameNode asking DataNodes to replicate a block below its target count.
postmortem.summary: The cluster experienced unplanned re-replication for block blk_-1009207079038502874, where the NameNode initiated replication requests to DataNodes that had fallen below their target replication factor. This activity was followed by the deletion of orphan replicas and intermittent write exceptions during serving attempts.
timeline: Multiple DataNodes received the block and added it to their blockMap (blk_-1009207079038502874#5, #6, #10, #14)
NameSystem asked 10.251.122.79:50010 to replicate the block to other datanodes (blk_-1009207079038502874#13)
Replication thread started and block was transmitted to 10.251.214.225:50010 (blk_-1009207079038502874#15, #19)
Orphan replicas were deleted from multiple DataNodes (blk_-1009207079038502874#28, #29, #30, #31, #32, #33)
Intermittent write exceptions occurred while serving the block to clients (blk_-1009207079038502874#21, #23, #25, #27)
recommended_actions: Let the replication monitor finish transferring the block.
Monitor the replication queue size to ensure transfers are keeping up.
Check which DataNode last held the block and whether it restarted recently.
If transfers remain slow, raise the replication stream limits temporarily.

RB-003#Symptom.text: Unplanned re-replication activity - Symptom: NameNode lines `ask <dn> to replicate blk_... to datanode(s) <dn2>` followed by `Starting thread to transfer block` and `Transmitted block` show the cluster copying a block because it fell below its replication target.

RB-015#Fix.text: Decommissioning DataNode stuck - Fix: Wait for replication to finish or close the blocking files.

RB-004#Fix.text: Block reported that belongs to no file - Fix: The NameNode instructs the DataNode to delete the orphan replica. No manual action is needed unless the reports keep coming.

RB-003#Checks.text:
Unplanned re-replication activity - Checks: 1. Check which DataNode last held the block and whether it restarted recently.
2. Look for earlier write exceptions for the same block (see RB-002).
3. Check the replication queue size and whether transfers are keeping up.

RB-003#Fix.text: Unplanned re-replication activity - Fix: Let the replication monitor finish. If transfers are slow, raise the replication stream limits temporarily. Confirm the block returns to its target replication count.
